pathogens.why: C. difficile is essentially the sole cause of antibiotic-associated colitis with this clinical pattern; testing (toxin EIA, PCR, or a two-step algorithm) confirms the diagnosis since asymptomatic colonization is common and should not be treated.

investigations.test: Stool C. difficile toxin EIA and/or PCR (per local two-step algorithm)
investigations.why: Confirms the diagnosis; testing only symptomatic patients (not all diarrhea, and never asymptomatic patients) avoids overdiagnosis of colonization.

investigations.test: Abdominal X-ray or CT (if severe/fulminant presentation suspected)
investigations.why: Screens for toxic megacolon or ileus, which would change management to include surgical involvement.
Supports severity classification (e.g., leukocytosis >15,000, rising creatinine define severe disease per IDSA criteria) which guides treatment intensity.
